Topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Predictive Logic

Target audience: University students (Introductory Statistics/Data Science)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Review: Conditional Probability

Lecture lines:
Conditional probability measures A given B occurred.
It restricts the sample space to event B.
Example: Knowing a card is Red changes probabilities.

Planned animations:
Display circle for Event A (#FF5733) and Event B (#33FF57).
Animate intersection of A and B as darker shade.
Show formula P(A|B) = P(A∩B)/P(B) near intersection.
Highlight event B area as the new sample space.
Fade out original sample space, focusing on P(A|B).

Section: section_2 — Defining Independence

Lecture lines:
Independent events share no predictive information.
Mathematically: P(A|B) equals P(A).
Example: Coin flips are unaffected by cats.

Planned animations:
Display two independent circles A and B.
Show P(A∩B) = P(A) * P(B) equation appear.
Flash circles to reinforce independent, non-overlapping probability logic.

Section: section_3 — Introduction to Bayes' Theorem

Lecture lines:
Bayes' theorem updates beliefs with new evidence.
Formula: Posterior equals Likelihood times Prior over Evidence.
It refines probability based on observed data.
Example: Sensor detections adjust disease likelihood.
It is the core of predictive logic.

Planned animations:
Display tree diagram starting from Event B.
Branch into Event A and not A.
Label branches with conditional probabilities P(A|B).

Section: section_4 — The Interaction: Independence vs. Bayes

Lecture lines:
Independent events make Bayes' theorem collapse.
If independent, P(A|B) simplifies to P(A).
New evidence becomes irrelevant to our prediction.
Example: Unrelated rain and weather apps.
Independence means no Bayesian update occurs.

Planned animations:
Show overlap of independent and dependent visual models.
Highlight area where P(A|B) collapses to P(A).
Display equation P(A|B) = P(A) for independence.

Section: section_5 — Summary & Real-World Application

Lecture lines:
Bayes' is for learning from evidence.
Independence means events offer no mutual insight.
Robots use Bayes, but ignore independent noise.

Planned animations:
Display real-world scenario (e.g., medical test) icons.
Connect test result icon to true status via probabilities.
Flash final summary text: Bayes' Theorem in practice.
